explanation: Neither document straddles the 2016-09-29 break date in a way that provides substantive new policy content on that date: the September 21 document held rates steady with incrementally hawkish language ('case for an increase has strengthened') but no rate change, and the November 2 document similarly held rates and reiterated the same gradual-tightening framework. The September 29 break date falls between these two meetings with no FOMC action or communication on that date; the market break more plausibly reflects the Deutsche Bank stress episode and associated global risk-off moves that occurred around that time, which are not captured in either FOMC document.
